walkthroughs.body_html: By 1917, Russia had lost about 1.7 million dead. Nicholas took personal command at the front in September 1915, leaving Alexandra and Rasputin as targets of court intrigue. Inflation eroded living standards; bread queues lengthened in Petrograd. The Progressive Bloc (1915) sought a 'ministry of confidence' but was rebuffed.

walkthroughs.h2: Five days that toppled the Tsar
walkthroughs.body_html: International Women's Day strikes (8 March 1917) ignited unrest. Within days the Petrograd garrison mutinied. The Duma's Provisional Committee and the new Petrograd Soviet emerged in parallel. Nicholas II's train was diverted to Pskov; he abdicated on 15 March 1917. The Provisional Government promised elections to a Constituent Assembly.

Lenin's April Theses demanded 'All Power to the Soviets'. The June Offensive collapsed; the July Days saw mass protest. The Kornilov Affair (August) discredited Kerensky; the Bolsheviks gained majorities in major Soviets. Trotsky's Military Revolutionary Committee orchestrated the seizure of key buildings on 25 October (OS) 1917; the Winter Palace fell that night. The Second Congress of Soviets ratified Decrees on Peace and Land.

mcqs.q: How did the Bolsheviks seize power in October 1917?
options: The October Revolution overthrew the Tsar.
Trotsky's Military Revolutionary Committee coordinated a near-bloodless takeover of key buildings in Petrograd from a Provisional Government that had lost army and worker support.
The Provisional Government fell because the Tsar returned and reclaimed his throne.
The October Revolution was a mass popular uprising that stormed the Winter Palace.

mcqs.q: Why did the Provisional Government fail in 1917?
options: The Provisional Government fell because the Tsar returned and reclaimed his throne.
Lenin personally led the storming of the Winter Palace.
It continued the unpopular war, did not redistribute land, shared 'dual power' with the Petrograd Soviet, and was discredited by the Kornilov affair before the Bolshevik takeover.
The Provisional Government fell because Lenin was personally more charismatic than Kerensky.

mcqs.q: What happened in the Russian Revolution of 1917?
options: Lenin personally led the storming of the Winter Palace.
The October Revolution overthrew the Tsar.
The Bolsheviks overthrew the Tsar in 1917.
There were two revolutions: February overthrew the Tsar and installed the Provisional Government; October saw the Bolsheviks seize power from that government.
